subject: Change the reactivity ordering in a Shiny

messages.author: ea6c79ef57d1267c
messages.subject: Change the reactivity ordering in a Shiny
parts:
Hi Folks,
 
I have used Rstudio Shiny package to develop a disease monitoring system. This system includes 55 diseases and three trigonometric models are used to monitor them. Since the behavior of each disease is different, the default delected model for each disease is different but known. e.g. "First order Trig model"' is better for Ecoli O157, "Second order" is better for Rocky Mountatin Fever, etc. However, the user can change the model to evaluate other models on a single disease type.
 
Since the codes for the system are too lengthy, i wrote a part of my ui.R and server. R codes: 
 
------------------------------------------------------------------------
ui.R
selectInput("disease", "Choose the disease:", choices=c( "Anaplasma Phagocytophilum", ...) ),
sliderInput( "L" , label="Factor for Control Limits",  min=2 , max=6 , value=3 , step=0.2 , animate=T) ,
...
uiOutput("degree"),
....
showOutput("myPlot", "highcharts")
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
server.R
 
  output$degree <- renderUI({
   
     if (input$disease %in% degreeZero) {
      selectInput("degree0", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="Zero Order Model")
    }
   
    else if (input$disease %in% degreeOne) {
        selectInput("degree1", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="First Order Model")
      } 
   
    else {
        selectInput("degree2", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="Second Order Model")
      }
   
  })
 
  output$myPlot <- renderChart2(
{
essentially employs the inputs and measure the control limits and spit out the Control Charts
}
 
-----------------------------------------------------------
 
and My Question is: when I change the disease names, The model computes control limits using the previous model and after a short bit of time it recognizes that the model type is also updated. I guess the reason is because of the reactivity order. I mean the package first updates the disease, then run the R codes and spit out outputs. Since one of the outputs is model type (uiOutput("degree") change, it reruns the R codes and show the new control chart.
 
Is there anyway in R shiny to ractive a special output before running R codes?
 
Thank you in advance,
Ehsan
